- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows upward momentum.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to inflated 30d forecasts; apply dampening factor to post-spike values.
- Mean reversion is evident when forecast diverges >20% from 14d moving average; adjust toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- Forecasts for 30d horizon are often too optimistic in high-sentiment periods; cap upper bounds at 1.5x recent 7d high if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment history shows repeated downward corrections (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or 0.33), model tends to underestimate; add 10–20% buffer to early forecast values.
